verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
verses.1:2: to the saints and faithful brethren in Christ in Colossae: Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: We give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always as we pray for you,
verses.1:4: having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love which you have toward all the saints,
verses.1:5: because of the hope stored up for you in the heavens, of which you heard beforehand in the word of the truth of the gospel,
verses.1:6: which has come to you, even as in all the world it is bearing fruit and increasing, as it also does among you from the day you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth;
verses.1:7: just as you learned from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on our behalf,
verses.1:8: who also made known to us your love in the Spirit.
verses.1:9: For this reason we also, from the day we heard it, do not cease praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the full knowledge of His will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
verses.1:10: so that you may walk worthy of the Lord, pleasing Him in every way, bearing fruit in every good work and increasing in the full knowledge of God;
verses.1:11: being strengthened with all power according to the might of His glory, for all endurance and longsuffering with joy,
verses.1:12: giving thanks to the Father, who has qualified you for the portion of the inheritance of the saints in the light,
verses.1:13: who delivered us out of the dominion of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of His love,
verses.1:14: in whom we have our redemption, the forgiveness of sins;
verses.1:15: who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation,
verses.1:16: for in Him all things were created in the heavens and upon the earth, things visible and things invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or authorities; all things have been created through Him and for Him.
verses.1:17: And He Himself is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.
verses.1:18: And He Himself is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from among the dead, that in all things He Himself may be preeminent.
verses.1:19: For it pleased God that all the fullness should dwell in Him,
verses.1:20: and through Him to reconcile all things to Himself, having made peace through the blood of His cross—through Him, whether things upon the earth or things in the heavens.
verses.1:21: And you, who once were alienated and enemies in your mind in wicked works—
verses.1:22: yet now you have been reconciled in the body of His flesh through death—to present you holy and blameless and above reproach in His sight,
verses.1:23: if indeed you continue in the faith, firmly founded and steadfast, and not shifting away from the hope of the gospel which you heard, which was proclaimed in all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.
verses.1:24: Now I rejoice in my sufferings on your behalf, and I fill up what remains lacking in the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for the sake of His body, which is the church,
verses.1:25: of which I became a minister according to the stewardship of God given to me for your sake, to fulfill the word of God,
verses.1:26: the mystery hidden from the ages and from the generations—yet now it has been made manifest to His saints,
verses.1:27: to whom God desired to make known what the riches of the glory of this mystery are among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
verses.1:28: Him we proclaim, admonishing every man and teaching every man in all wisdom, so that we may present every man mature in Christ.
verses.1:29: For this I also labor, striving according to His working which works in me with power.
verses.2:1: For I desire you to know how great a conflict I have on behalf of you and of those in Laodicea, and of all who have not seen my face in the flesh,
verses.2:2: so that their hearts may be encouraged, knit together in love and reaching all the riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the full knowledge of the mystery of God, that is, Christ,
verses.2:3: in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge lie hidden.
verses.2:4: This I say lest anyone delude you with persuasive speech.
verses.2:5: For even though I am absent in the flesh, yet I am with you in spirit, rejoicing and beholding your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
verses.2:6: As therefore you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in Him,
verses.2:7: having been rooted and being built up in Him, and established in the faith just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.
verses.2:8: Beware lest anyone carry you off captive through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the elementary principles of the world, and not according to Christ.
verses.2:9: For in Him all the fullness of the Godhead dwells in bodily form,
verses.2:10: and in Him you have been made full, who is the head of every principality and authority,
verses.2:11: in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ,
verses.2:12: having been buried together with Him in baptism, in which you were also raised together with Him through faith in the working of God, who raised Him from among the dead.
verses.2:13: And you, who were dead in your transgressions and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, He made alive together with Him, having freely forgiven us all our transgressions,
verses.2:14: having blotted out the written bond with its decrees that stood against us, which was opposed to us; and He has taken it out of the way, nailing it to the cross.
verses.2:15: Having disarmed the principalities and the authorities, He made an open display of them, triumphing over them in it.
verses.2:16: Therefore let no one judge you in food and in drink, or in the matter of a festival or a new moon or Sabbaths,
verses.2:17: which are a shadow of the things that are to come, while the substance belongs to Christ.
verses.2:18: Let no one rob you of your prize, delighting in self-abasement and the worship of angels, entering into the things which he has seen, puffed up without cause by the mind of his flesh,
verses.2:19: and not holding fast the Head, from whom the entire body, supplied and knit together through the joints and ligaments, increases with the growth that comes from God.
verses.2:20: If you died with Christ from the elementary principles of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you submit yourselves to decrees:
verses.2:21: "Do not handle, nor taste, nor touch,"
verses.2:22: all of which perish with use, according to the commandments and teachings of men?
verses.2:23: Such things indeed carry a show of wisdom in self-made worship and self-abasement and unsparing severity toward the body, yet they are of no value against the gratification of the flesh.
verses.3:1: Therefore, if you were raised together with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ is, sitting at the right hand of God.
verses.3:2: Fix your minds on the things above, not on the things upon the earth.
verses.3:3: For you have died, and your life lies hidden with Christ in God.
verses.3:4: When Christ, who is your life, is manifested, then you also shall be manifested with Him in glory.
verses.3:5: Therefore put to death the members that are upon the earth: fornication, impurity, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry.
verses.3:6: On account of these things the wrath of God is coming.
verses.3:7: In them you also once walked, when you were living in these things.
verses.3:8: But now you also lay aside all these things: anger, fury, malice, slander, and shameful speech from your mouth.
verses.3:9: Do not lie to one another, since you have stripped off the old man with his deeds,
verses.3:10: and have clothed yourselves with the new man, who is being renewed to true knowledge according to the image of Him who created him,
verses.3:11: where there is no Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, bondservant, or freeman; but Christ is all, and in all.
verses.3:12: Clothe yourselves therefore, as the chosen of God, holy and beloved, with a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, and longsuffering,
verses.3:13: bearing with one another and forgiving each other, if anyone has a grievance against another; just as the Lord also graciously forgave you, so you also must do.
verses.3:14: And over all these things clothe yourselves with love, which is the bond of perfection.
verses.3:15: And let the peace of Christ preside in your hearts, to which you were also called in one body; and be thankful.
verses.3:16: Let the word of Christ dwell richly in you in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs in grace, singing in your hearts to God.
verses.3:17: And all that you do, whether in word or in deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, offering thanks to God the Father through Him.
verses.3:18: Wives, submit yourselves to your husbands, as is proper in the Lord.
verses.3:19: Husbands, love your wives, and do not grow bitter toward them.
verses.3:20: Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is well-pleasing in the Lord.
verses.3:21: Fathers, do not provoke your children, lest they grow disheartened.
verses.3:22: Bondservants, obey your masters according to the flesh in everything, not with eye-service, as pleasers of men, but with singleness of heart, fearing the Lord.
verses.3:23: Whatever you do, work from the soul, as to the Lord and not to men,
verses.3:24: knowing that from the Lord you shall receive the recompense of the inheritance; it is the Lord Christ whom you serve.
verses.3:25: For he who does wrong shall receive back the wrong he has committed, and there is no partiality.
verses.4:1: Masters, render to your bondservants what is just and equitable, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.
verses.4:2: Persevere in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgiving,
verses.4:3: praying at the same time for us also, that God may open for us a door for the word, to declare the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds,
verses.4:4: so that I may manifest it as I ought to speak.
verses.4:5: Walk in wisdom toward outsiders, redeeming the time.
verses.4:6: Let your speech always be in grace, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer every person.
verses.4:7: Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister and fellow bondservant in the Lord, will make known to you everything concerning me,
verses.4:8: whom I have sent to you for this very purpose, that you may know our circumstances and that he may comfort your hearts,
verses.4:9: together with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of your own. They will make known to you everything that is happening here.
verses.4:10: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, sends greetings to you, and Mark, the cousin of Barnabas (concerning whom you received instructions: if he comes to you, receive him),
verses.4:11: and Jesus who is called Justus. Of those from the circumcision, these alone are fellow workers for the kingdom of God, who have become a consolation to me.
verses.4:12: Epaphras, who is one of your own, a bondservant of Christ Jesus, sends greetings to you, always wrestling fervently for you in his prayers, that you may stand complete and fully assured in all the will of God.
verses.4:13: For I testify on his behalf that he has great toil for you, and for those in Laodicea, and for those in Hierapolis.
verses.4:14: Luke, the beloved physician, sends greetings to you, and Demas also.
verses.4:15: Give greetings to the brethren in Laodicea, and to Nympha and the church in her house.
verses.4:16: And when this epistle has been read among you, see to it that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you also read the one from Laodicea.
verses.4:17: And say to Archippus, "Attend to the ministry that you received in the Lord, that you may fulfill it."
verses.4:18: This greeting is by my own hand—Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you.

notes.1:7: The critical Greek text reads "on our behalf" (representing Paul and his coworkers), whereas some later manuscripts read "on your behalf."
notes.1:12: The critical Greek text reads "you" here before shifting to "us" in verse 13; other manuscripts harmonize verse 12 to "us."
notes.1:19: The Greek verb "was pleased" has no explicit noun subject; "God" is supplied as the implied masculine subject required by the masculine participle "having made peace" in verse 20, though some take "all the fullness" as the subject.
notes.1:22: Following the critical Greek passive verb "you have been reconciled," verses 21-22 contain an abrupt grammatical shift marked by dashes; other manuscripts read the active "He has reconciled."
notes.2:2: The critical Greek text reads concisely "the mystery of God, Christ," placing Christ in apposition to the mystery; later manuscripts expand this to "of God, both of the Father and of Christ."
notes.2:8: The Greek phrase rendered "the elementary principles of the world" can denote either rudimentary religious teachings and cosmic elements or elemental spirits thought to rule the cosmos (compare verse 20).
notes.2:15: The closing Greek phrase may be translated either "in it" (referring back to the cross in verse 14) or "in Him" (referring to Christ).
notes.2:18: The critical Greek text reads "entering into the things which he has seen," alluding to claimed visionary experiences; later manuscripts insert a negative to read "things which he has not seen."
notes.2:23: The final Greek clause is compressed and debated, and may be read either as "of no value against the gratification of the flesh" or as "of no true honor, serving only to gratify the flesh."
notes.3:6: The critical Greek text omits the phrase "upon the sons of disobedience," which appears in some later manuscripts (likely assimilated from Ephesians 5:6).
notes.3:13: The Greek text reads "the Lord" (κύριος) rather than "Christ" or "God," which appear as variants in other manuscripts.
notes.3:16: The Greek punctuation joins "in all wisdom" with the indwelling of Christ's word, though it can alternatively modify "teaching and admonishing." The critical text also reads "to God" rather than "to the Lord."
notes.3:24: The verb "serve" (δουλεύετε) may be understood either as an indicative ("it is the Lord Christ whom you serve") or as an imperative ("Serve the Lord Christ!").
notes.4:8: The critical Greek text reads "that you may know our circumstances" (second person plural), whereas other manuscripts read "that he may know your circumstances."
notes.4:13: The critical Greek text reads "great toil" (πόνον) rather than "great zeal" (ζῆλον), which appears in later manuscripts.
notes.4:15: The feminine pronoun "her house" (αὐτῆς) identifies Νύμφαν as a woman named Nympha; some manuscripts read the masculine pronoun "his," taking the name as Nymphas.
notes.4:16: The letter "from Laodicea" is not preserved under that title; scholars have variously suggested it was a lost Pauline epistle or a circular letter such as Ephesians.
